title: Rules and Cooperation: Building the Conscience Before Behavior
summary: Between the ages of 4-6, the child begins to distinguish 'halal' from 'haram' (Erikson: Initiative vs Guilt), and the nucleus of their conscience takes shape. Guidance here is not through scolding but by involving them in setting rules: 'What do the two of us agree not to do while playing?' Recent research in positive parenting (CDC 2020) indicates that a child who participates in setting rules adheres to them more than a child who receives them as commands. The lesson presents the parent with the 'Mutual Contract' approach—3 clear rules that everyone in the family commits to.
try_this: This week: Sit with your child for 10 minutes and agree on 3 rules for play (e.g., 'We do not hit,' 'We take turns,' 'We ask before taking'). Write them on a paper and hang it up. Every time the child adheres to a rule, praise their behavior specifically ('I liked that you asked before taking the toy'). At the end of the week, review together: Which rule did we adhere to the most?
reflection_prompts: Have you noticed your child suggesting rules you hadn’t thought of?
When did you feel that your commitment to the rules was harder than your child’s?
